note: PiCode's own pi, pinned to an exact version so a freshly built editor is born working. `build/pi-runtime.sh` installs it during the build and the connector looks for it there — nobody has to install or configure it. **1.3.0 → 1.4.0, a normal step**: the 1.4.0 changelog carries no breaking-changes section at all, and nothing it does change is a surface this product stands on. PiCode registers exactly two extension events, `before_agent_start` and `tool_call`, so the new attribution-header rules for `before_provider_headers` never reach it, and it sends no attribution headers of its own. `generateSummary()` and its `reserveTokens` argument are not called here. Nothing imports `@earendil-works/pi-ai/models`, the codemode classifiers and their new `images` input are unused, and the Rex terminal does not exist in a VS Code workbench. The provider attribution and default-model moves (GitHub Copilot's retired `gpt-5.4` → `gpt-6.1-sol`, the NVIDIA and Xiaomi defaults) cannot leave a stale name on screen either: the model picker reads pi's catalogue live instead of pinning one. What does reach the owner is Windows-shaped and lands on the buttons that exist: `pi update` no longer fails with “Managed install marker is missing or invalid” when `managed-install.json` begins with a UTF-8 BOM, which PowerShell 5.1 writes by itself — that is the Update button in the Updates card and the notification's; `mcp.json` with a BOM parses again, and PiCode writes that file as plain text while another tool may not; shell detection finds PowerShell outside `PATH`, so the agent's own shell starts on machines where it used to fail; and `grep` now runs `rg --no-config`, so a `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` on the machine can no longer turn a regex search into a literal one behind the model's back. The rest is inside the agent: compaction summaries use the model's output limit instead of a fixed cap, and codemode scripts queue for a worker for up to 60 seconds instead of failing. Catalog additions the picker will simply show: `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, and `xhigh` thinking on Grok 4.3 and 4.5. Verified against the 1.4.0 tarball before pinning: `dist/index.js` exports `createAgentSessionServices`, `createAgentSessionFromServices` and `SessionManager`, `dist/cli.js` is present, and `dist/extensions/index.js` carries its four built-ins (`llama.cpp`, `codemode`, `tool-search`, `mcp`), each with the `builtin: true` mark the connector's own reader requires; `@earendil-works/pi-mcp` is pinned to 1.4.0 alongside it, so its `dist/oauth` entry matches too. The audits of the earlier steps (1.1.0 → 1.2.0, 1.2.0 → 1.3.0) were written the same way and live in this file's git history.
